MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the largest number: 3,060, 3,006, 3,600, 3,660? (1 mark)
   A. 3,600
   B. 3,060
   C. 3,660
   D. 3,006

2. Which of these is a factor of 40? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 10
   C. 6
   D. 3

3. How many factors does 12 have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 7

4. Which number is written in words as "six thousand and forty-five"? (1 mark)
   A. 645
   B. 6,045
   C. 60,405
   D. 6,405

5. Work out 3,568 + 2,276. (1 mark)
   A. 5,744
   B. 5,734
   C. 5,854
   D. 5,844

6. Which number must be added to 2,318 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 3,415
   B. 3,425
   C. 8,061
   D. 3,525

7. Work out 7,865 − 3,542. (1 mark)
   A. 4,333
   B. 5,323
   C. 4,323
   D. 4,223

8. Change 5 1/2 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 6/2
   B. 11/2
   C. 10/2
   D. 12/2

9. Change 22/7 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/7
   B. 3 1/7
   C. 1 3/7
   D. 3 2/7

10. Change 1 5/6 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 11/7
   B. 12/6
   C. 6/6
   D. 11/6

11. What is 3/8 of 40? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 15
   C. 5
   D. 20

12. Which is the smallest number: 0.3, 0.29, 0.31, 0.03? (1 mark)
   A. 0.3
   B. 0.03
   C. 0.31
   D. 0.29

13. In the number 5.68, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Tenths
   C. Hundredths
   D. Ones

14. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 3.09? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 0.009
   C. 0.9
   D. 0.09

15. If n = 6, what is the value of n + 5? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 30
   C. 1
   D. 65

16. Why can 2a + 3b not be written as 5ab? (1 mark)
   A. Because 2 + 3 is not 5
   B. Because letters can only be added to numbers
   C. Because ab is not a letter
   D. a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined

17. A fence uses 4 pieces of wire, each 2 m 30 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 9 m 10 cm
   B. 2 m 34 cm
   C. 9 m 20 cm
   D. 10 m 20 cm

18. What is 2 m 90 cm + 3 m 30 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 7 m 20 cm
   B. 6 m 10 cm
   C. 6 m 20 cm
   D. 5 m 20 cm

19. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 26 cm
   B. 40 cm
   C. 13 cm
   D. 28 cm

20. Rectangle P has 3 rows and 10 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 5 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle Q
   B. It cannot be told
   C. They are equal
   D. Rectangle P

21. How many quarter-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 8
   D. 2

22. An electronic balance shows 0.75 kg. Which mass is this? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/2 kg
   B. 3/4 kg
   C. 1/4 kg
   D. 1/2 kg

23. A learner goes to bed at nine o'clock at night. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 9:00 p.m.
   B. 9:30 p.m.
   C. 9:00 a.m.
   D. 9:00 noon

24. How many minutes are in 8 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 800 minutes
   B. 480 minutes
   C. 192 minutes
   D. 540 minutes

25. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 95, Ksh 140 and Ksh 260. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 495
   B. Ksh 595
   C. Ksh 505
   D. Ksh 395

26. How many cents are in Ksh 5? (1 mark)
   A. 500 cents
   B. 5,000 cents
   C. 105 cents
   D. 50 cents

27. 2,005 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 200.50
   B. Ksh 20.05
   C. Ksh 21.05
   D. Ksh 2

28. Which statement about a rectangle is true? (1 mark)
   A. It has a curved edge
   B. All sides are always equal
   C. It has three sides
   D. Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles

29. In a tally chart, one group of five and 3 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 9
   C. 13
   D. 8

30. What should every good table have? (1 mark)
   A. A title and column headings
   B. No numbers
   C. A long story
   D. Only pictures

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. The table shows football 5, netball 3, athletics 1 and swimming 1 for 10 pupils. Which sport is the most popular? How many pupils chose netball or athletics? (3 marks)

32. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there altogether? (3 marks)

33. A rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. Peter walks once round the plot. How far does he walk? (3 marks)

34. Explain why the parts must be equal when we write a fraction such as 1/4. (2 marks)

35. Explain how you would find the lines of symmetry of a paper rectangle. How many are there? (4 marks)

36. Find the first common multiple of 4 and 6 by writing the first six multiples of each number. (4 marks)

37. Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. How many whole oranges is that? Write your answer as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

38. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. Find its perimeter. (3 marks)

39. A book cover has 12 rows of 9 squares. A notebook cover has 10 rows of 10 squares. Which cover is larger and by how many squares? (4 marks)

40. Describe how to make a 1/2 kg mass from sand using a 1 kg mass and a beam balance. (4 marks)

41. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact product. (4 marks)

42. A matatu carries m passengers. At a stop 8 get in and 3 get out. Write and simplify an expression for the number of passengers now. (3 marks)

43. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 blocks long, 3 wide and 2 high is 9 blocks because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What mistake did the learner make and what is the correct volume? (3 marks)

44. Write the decimal 5.68 in a place value chart and say the place value of the 6 and of the 8. (4 marks)

45. Mr Otieno has Ksh 2,000. He buys items costing Ksh 1,340. Does he have enough money? How much is left? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 3,660
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 3,660.

2. B — 10
   40 ÷ 10 = 4 with nothing left over, so 10 is a factor of 40. The others leave a remainder.

3. A — 6
   The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. There are 6 of them.

4. B — 6,045
   six thousand and forty-five: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 6,045.

5. D — 5,844
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,568 + 2,276 = 5,844.

6. B — 3,425
   5,743 − 2,318 = 3,425. Check: 2,318 + 3,425 = 5,743.

7. C — 4,323
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323. Check: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865.

8. B — 11/2
   5 × 2 = 10 and 10 + 1 = 11. The denominator stays 2, so the answer is 11/2.

9. B — 3 1/7
   22 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/7, so 22/7 = 3 1/7.

10. D — 11/6
   1 × 6 = 6 and 6 + 5 = 11. The denominator stays 6, so the answer is 11/6.

11. B — 15
   40 ÷ 8 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/8 of 40 is 15.

12. B — 0.03
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 0.03.

13. B — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 5.68 the digit 6 is in the tenths place.

14. D — 0.09
   The digit 9 is in the hundredths place, so its total value is 0.09.

15. A — 11
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 11.

16. D — a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined
   a and b stand for different kinds of things, so 2a and 3b are not like terms. The expression stays as 2a + 3b.

17. C — 9 m 20 cm
   230 × 4 = 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm.

18. C — 6 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 290 + 330 = 620 cm = 6 m 20 cm.

19. A — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.

20. C — They are equal
   P = 3 × 10 = 30 and Q = 6 × 5 = 30. They are equal.

21. A — 4
   Four quarters make one whole, so four 1/4 L containers make 1 L.

22. B — 3/4 kg
   0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4, so it is 3/4 kg.

23. A — 9:00 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 9:00 p.m..

24. B — 480 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 8 × 60 = 480 minutes.

25. A — Ksh 495
   Add the three costs: 95 + 140 + 260 = 495.

26. A — 500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 5 = 5 × 100 = 500 cents.

27. B — Ksh 20.05
   2,005 ÷ 100 = 20 remainder 5, so it is Ksh 20.05.

28. D — Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A rectangle has four sides, opposite sides equal and four right angles.

29. D — 8
   1 × 5 + 3 = 8.

30. A — A title and column headings
   A title tells what the table is about and headings tell what each column shows.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Football is the most popular. 3 + 1 = 4 pupils chose netball or athletics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for football, 1 mark for 3 + 1, 1 mark for 4.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: 630 bananas
   Working / marking points: 18 × 5 = 90 (1 mark); 18 × 30 = 540 (1 mark); 90 + 540 = 630 (1 mark).

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 40 m
   Working / marking points: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. 1 mark for identifying perimeter, 1 mark for the sum, 1 mark for unit.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different in size, one part is not one quarter of the whole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying parts must be equal in size and 1 mark for the reason.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fold the rectangle so that the two halves match. There are two folds that work: along the middle from top to bottom and along the middle from side to side. So there are 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding, 1 mark for halves matching, 1 mark for each of the two lines (or 2 marks for saying 2 with reasons).

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The first common multiple is 12.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct list and 2 marks for identifying 12.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/2 oranges
   Working / marking points: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1 (2 marks); 4 1/2 (1 mark).

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 m
   Working / marking points: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m. 2 marks for adding all six sides, 1 mark for the unit.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: The book cover: 108 squares. The notebook: 100 squares. The book cover is larger by 8 squares.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for 108 and 100, 1 mark for the larger cover, 1 mark for 8.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Balance a bag of sand against the 1 kg mass. Share the sand equally into two bags, checking with the balance that they are level. Each bag is 1/2 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balancing sand with 1 kg, 1 mark for sharing into two bags, 1 mark for checking they balance, 1 mark for stating each is 1/2 kg.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 40 × 20 = 800. Exact: 836.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding to 40 and 20, 1 mark for 800, 1 mark for 38 × 2 = 76 and 38 × 20 = 760, 1 mark for 836.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: m + 8 − 3 = m + 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for m + 8, 1 mark for taking away 3, 1 mark for simplifying to m + 5.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: The learner added. She should multiply: one layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks and 2 layers make 24 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for 24 blocks.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ones 5, tenths 6, hundredths 8. The 6 is in the tenths place and the 8 is in the hundredths place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct chart, 1 mark for each place value, 1 mark for using the decimal point correctly.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Yes. He has Ksh 660 left.
   Working / marking points: 2,000 is more than 1,340 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,340 (1 mark); Ksh 660 (1 mark).
